correctness.rationale: For xdot=x[r(1-x/K)x/(x+c)-g] with r,K,c,g>0, the per-capita untreatened growth r phi(x) is maximized at x*=sqrt[c(K+c)]-c, since phi'(x)=(Kc-2cx-x^2)/(K(x+c)^2). Its maximum is (sqrt(K+c)-sqrt(c))^2/K. Hence global asymptotic attraction to zero for all x>=0 holds iff g>gc=r(sqrt(K+c)-sqrt(c))^2/K; at equality x* is a positive equilibrium, below equality exactly two positive roots with lower unstable and upper locally attracting. Independently derived quadratic equilibrium discriminant and checked K=2,c=1,r=3/25 gives gc=r(2-sqrt3) and same root regimes. Strict positivity and long-term constant-treatment qualifier are necessary.
